courses.title: Urban Inquiry & Practice
courses.description: Effective inquiries in urban studies require the application of approaches to find, analyze, and communicate data about the city, its residents, and its functions. From these applications, they can become the keys to professional urban practices in careers that focus on examining cities.

courses.title: STT-Intro Age-Friendly Cities
courses.description: Introduces age-friendly cities and communities through urban studies and gerontology. Students explore how neighbourhoods, services, policies, and everyday environments shape aging, with attention to WHO age-friendly domains, healthy aging, sustainability, equity, inclusion, and community change.

courses.title: Indig City: Transf Storyscapes
courses.description: Creative, critical ‘reading’ of the colonialism embedded within the stories, landscapes, and systems of the Canadian city, and the foundational place of Indigenous planning, laws, stories, and cultures in shaping sustainable decolonial futures. Focuses on Vancouver and its journey to being a “City of Reconciliation”, in the context of UNDRIP.

courses.title: Urban Lab
courses.prerequisiteText: 60 units and permission of the instructor. Students should seek permission from the instructor prior to the term in which they wish to enroll.
courses.description: Immersive capstone experience in organizational change processes with external urban laboratory organization. Students will learn and apply understandings of urban innovation, systemic and transformational change, and sustainability transitions. The lab course will consist of lectures, discussions and exercises, intensive reading, extensive time in the field, and preparing a team-based project.
